document.title: Official Informal for SA Assistant Secretary Robin Raphel and SA/PAB (Islama 01873)
document.publisher: National Security Archive (GWU), Pakistan: "The Taliban's Godfather"?
document.note: [Confidential] Fighting will continue as Iran and Russia supply Massoud, while Pakistan appears to review its policy but agencies like ISID remain committed to a Taliban victory. The Taliban continue to protect bin Laden and appear to have a deal, perhaps ISID-brokered, letting HUA use Khost camps. The Embassy recommends limited engagement.

events.description: US Embassy Islamabad sends an Official Informal cable proposing a 'restrained engagement' policy to moderate and modernize the Taliban.
Planned testimony by Robin Raphel on the Hill.
Taliban claim of 'total victory' by the next Eid, mid-April.
Raphel's remarks at the UN stressing Taliban work with UN envoy Holl.

US Embassy Islamabad sends official informal cable (sections 3 and 4) to State recommending steps on Taliban policy: expel bin Ladin, OIC engagement, clerical visits, Russia/Central Asia dialogue, UN support, reconstruction escrow fund.
Proposal to approach OIC and Saudi Arabia/Egypt to engage Mullah Omar and Taliban on a negotiated settlement.
Proposed Afghanistan Reconstruction Escrow Fund, disbursed once a broad-based government is established.
US Embassy Islamabad sends Official Informal cable to Raphel on Taliban and proposed 'restrained engagement' policy.
Planned testimony on the Hill by Assistant Secretary Raphel.
Raphel's remarks at the UN urging Taliban to work with Holl.
Taliban claim 'total victory' by next Eid, mid-April; fighting expected to intensify.
War fought on Bamian/Parwan and Badghis fronts.

key_claims: The Embassy assesses that the Taliban have not negotiated in good faith in UN talks and use them as cover for military advances.
The Taliban continue to shelter Osama bin Ladin, despite claims they told him not to engage in terrorism.
The Taliban appear to have a deal, perhaps brokered by ISID, letting Harakat-ul-Ansar use Khost camps.
ISID appears committed to a Taliban victory even as Pakistan reviews its Afghan policy.
The Taliban are not monolithic, but are a lasting fact of life in Afghanistan.
The Embassy recommends 'restrained engagement' to moderate the Taliban rather than isolation or all-out engagement.
Pakistan is seen as the Taliban's diplomatic and political sponsor and tacit materiel supplier, and the US should press the new Sharif government to use its leverage.
